1 قَزَحَ القِدْرَ : see 2. ＝
-A2- قَزَحَتِ القِدْرُ, [aor.
قَزَحَ ,] inf. n. قَزْحٌ and قَزَحَانٌ, The cooking-pot made what came forth [or overflowed] from it to drip, or fall in drops. (AZ, K, TA.) ―
-b2- And قَزَحَ بِبَوْلِهِ, (S, A, Mgh, K,) and قَزِحَ بِهِ, (A, Mgh, K,) aor. of each
قَزَحَ , (K,) inf. n. قَزْحٌ (S, K) and قُزُوحٌ; (K;) and به ↓ قزّح , inf. n. تَقْزِيحٌ; (A;) said of a dog, (S, A, Mgh, K,) He ejected his urine, (S, Mgh, TA,) and sprinkled it: (S:) or raised his hind leg, and emitted his urine: (TA:) or ejected his urine with an impetus, or in several discharges. (K, accord. to different copies; as is said in the TA.) ―
-b3- قَزَحَ أَصْلَ الشَّجَرَةِ: see 2. ＝
-A3- قَزَحَ also signifies It (a thing, TA) was or became, high, or elevated. (K, TA.) ―
-b2- And قَزَحَتْ, said of a plant or tree [نَبْتَةٌ or شَحَرَةٌ], It had, or produced, what is termed a تَقْزِيح [q. v.]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
